title: eviction-thermostat-adaptive-backoff-probe-integration
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds an adaptive eviction thermostat to smooth regional failover and reduces cascading evictions during transient health flaps. Backport-ready hotfix for recent incident; safe rollout via feature flag.
description:
Context: Recent incident (see ENG-2491) showed cascading pod/node evictions when a regional egress flap produced short-lived health failures. This caused SLO violations across dependent routes as the scheduler aggressively reclaimed capacity. Goal: introduce a lightweight admission controller ("eviction thermostat") and tie it to our regional health probes so eviction decisions incorporate probe health and a dynamically tuned cooling window.

What this PR does: - Implements an eviction thermostat that applies an adaptive backoff (cooling period) after an eviction event; backoff increases with eviction rate and decays over time. - Integrates the thermostat with regional health probe signals so temporarily degraded regions avoid aggressive eviction unless probe indicates sustained failure. - Adds a probe reconciliation path: when probe client reports intermittent failures but node-level metrics are healthy, the thermostat biases towards softer admission (prefer delaying eviction). - Adds new observability hooks and SLI counters (thermostat_evictions, thermostat_backoff_seconds, probe_influence_score) and a runbook doc. - Wires feature flag `eviction_thermostat.v1` for staged rollout and a hotfix deployment script.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for thermostat logic [x] integration test with simulated probe flaps [x] alerts updated [x] docs/runbook added [x] feature-flag gating and k8s rollout script

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: over-retaining unhealthy workloads. Mitigation: thermostat consults node-level health and will allow eviction when node metrics cross critical thresholds; emergency bypass flag `eviction_thermostat.force_evict` included. - Risk: subtle interaction with existing autoscaler. Mitigation: added deterministic ordering (eviction first consults thermostat, then autoscaler) and integration tests to verify ordering.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature flag in staging and run soak tests for 48h. 2) Canary enable in a single region (non-critical) and monitor thermostat_evictions and SLO error budget burn. 3) Gradual ramp across regions with a 4h observation window per stage. 4) In case of unexpected retention, flip `eviction_thermostat.force_evict` to restore prior behavior.

Metrics to watch: thermostat_evictions, thermostat_backoff_seconds, regional_probe_flap_count, request_latency_p50/p95 for affected routes, error_budget_burn_rate.

Related: ENG-2491, runbook link: docs/runbooks/eviction-thermostat.md
